pages.text: In the back room, Grandpa poured stove-warmed water into a big basin. A line of steam rose. "Who wants a bath?" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, squirmed.
"I hate wet fur! I hate water in my ears!" Kiki pulled a towel over the head and scurried to the stove. "I will stay warm here!"
After a while, the fur felt stiff and itchy. Rolling snow all day had left ash and dirt in it. "Why am I so grubby?"
Grandpa beckoned from the back room with soap and a toy duck. "Forget a bath—want to visit Steam Land?" Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, and Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, followed.
Grandpa stirred the water. Bubbles rose like mountains, and steam turned the back room white. "Wow! It really is Steam Land!" Kiki's eyes widened.
"There is an order in Steam Land. Feet in gently, then down to your shoulders!" Grandpa hung Kiki's green bell on a nail. Nono and Gugu called, "Into the warm water—splash!"
Kiki eased in feet first, then down to the shoulders. Nono poured water from a cup. Gugu waited with a towel. Soapy bubbles and splashes with the duck! "Into the warm water—splash!"
Out of the basin, the fur was fluffy, with wisps of steam rising. "Warmer than the stove, right?" Gugu opened the towel wide. Kiki put the green bell back on and touched it.
Next night, when the awning came down, Kiki ran to the back room first. "One, feet in gently! Two, bubbly soap! Three, pour water to rinse!" Nono and Gugu queued with towels.
Grandpa hugged Kiki snugly in the towel. Washing in warm water keeps you warm longest. "Steam Land again tomorrow night! Into the warm water—splash!" Kiki said.
